question.problem:
Which of the following products is the LU factorization of a matrix $A?$

I. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$

II. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$

III. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that in the LU factorization of a matrix $A,$ we write $A=LU$ where the matrix $L$ is a unit lower triangular matrix (a lower triangular matrix that has only $1$'s on the main diagonal) and the matrix $U$ is an upper triangular matrix:

$$
A=\overset{L}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ ∗ & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{U}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]}}
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each product in turn.

- The first product is in $LU$ form because the left matrix is a unit lower triangular matrix, and the right matrix is an upper triangular matrix.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

- The second product is *not* in $LU$ form because the matrix on the left is not a unit lower triangular matrix, as its main diagonal contains a number not equal to $1.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\,\times 
$$

- The third product is *not* in $LU$ form because the matrix on the right is not an upper triangular matrix, as it has a non-zero entry below the diagonal.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,\times 
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
